claims.claim: Grey County Council closed its 2023-2026 term on November 12 and bid farewell to ten members who are not returning.
claims.episode_span: closed its 2023-2026 term on November 12 and bid farewell to ten members who are not returning
claims.source_title: Grey County warden proud of accomplishments of outgoing council
claims.supporting_quote: Grey County Council closed out its 2023–2026 term on November 12 with an emotional farewell to 10 departing councillors and a look back at four years of infrastructure, healthcare, and regional initiatives.

claims.claim: Bronze service pins went to Andrea Matrosovs, Ross Kentner and Dane Nielsen after four years, Peter Bordignon after five, and Terry McKay and Tom Hutchinson after eight; silver pins went to Sue Paterson, Ian Boddy and Scott Mackey after twelve years and Brian Milne after sixteen.
claims.episode_span: Bronze pins went to Warden Andrea Matrosovs, Ross Kentner and Dane Nielsen after four years
claims.source_title: Grey County warden proud of accomplishments of outgoing council
claims.supporting_quote: Bronze pins went to four-year members Warden Andrea Matrosovs, Ross Kentner, and Dane Nielsen, five-year member Peter Bordignon, and eight-year veterans Terry McKay and Tom Hutchinson. Silver pins were awarded to 12-year councillors Sue Paterson, Ian Boddy, and Scott Mackey, as well as Deputy Warden Brian Milne, who served for 16 years.

claims.claim: Warden Andrea Matrosovs said Rockwood Terrace is 75 per cent complete ahead of a planned 2027 opening, and that Lee Manor was one of 17 Ontario long-term care homes to receive provincial dementia-care funding.
claims.episode_span: Rockwood Terrace, 75 per cent complete ahead of a planned 2027 opening
claims.source_title: Grey County warden proud of accomplishments of outgoing council
claims.supporting_quote: She noted that the Rockwood Terrace redevelopment project is 75 per cent complete ahead of its planned 2027 opening, while Lee Manor was named one of just 17 long-term care homes in Ontario to receive provincial dementia care funding.

claims.claim: Matrosovs said the Durham paramedic base opened in September 2025 and Feversham in October 2026, and that paramedics met or exceeded most response-time targets despite a 9 per cent increase in calls.
claims.episode_span: the Durham paramedic base opened in September 2025 and Feversham in October 2026
claims.source_title: Grey County warden proud of accomplishments of outgoing council
claims.supporting_quote: Not only did we open the Durham base officially in September of 2025, but just recently we opened Feversham in October 2026, and the paramedics met or exceeded most of the response time targets even though there was a 9% increase in calls,

claims.claim: Colour It Home, a 10-year housing strategy, was introduced in April 2026 after more than 1,000 additional nights of shelter, and a road-transfer agreement takes legal effect on June 1, 2027.
claims.episode_span: Colour It Home, a 10-year housing and homelessness strategy introduced in April 2026
claims.source_title: Grey County warden proud of accomplishments of outgoing council
claims.supporting_quote: In April 2026, the county introduced Colour It Home, a new 10-year housing and homelessness strategy focused on increasing housing supply, early intervention, and equitable support, following a year that saw more than 1,000 additional nights of shelter provided.

claims.claim: A 60-year-old school bus driver was seriously injured in a crash with a transport truck near Stayner, and the Simcoe Muskoka Catholic District School Board said no students were on the bus.
claims.episode_span: A 60-year-old school bus driver was seriously injured in a crash with a transport truck near Stayner
claims.source_title: 60-year-old bus driver seriously injured after crash with transport truck near Stayner
claims.supporting_quote: The Simcoe Muskoka Catholic District School Board said there were no students were on the bus.

claims.claim: OPP were called just before 7 a.m. to Highway 26 between Centre Line Road and 3-4 Sideroad near Stayner, and the bus driver was taken to hospital.
claims.episode_span: OPP were called just before 7 a.m. to Highway 26 between Centre Line Road and 3-4 Sideroad
claims.source_title: School bus driver hurt in collision near Stayner
claims.supporting_quote: Emergency services were called just before 7 a.m. to Highway 26 between Centre Line Road and 3-4 Sideroad near Stayner.

claims.claim: The Stayner roadway later reopened after the school bus and transport truck crash.
claims.episode_span: Simcoe.com later reported the Stayner roadway had reopened.
claims.source_title: UPDATED: Stayner roadway reopens after Monday morning crash between school bus, transport truck
claims.supporting_quote: UPDATED: Stayner roadway reopens after Monday morning crash between school bus, transport truck

claims.claim: Collingwood's winter parking restrictions are in place and no overnight street parking is allowed until April.
claims.episode_span: No overnight street parking is allowed until April.
claims.source_title: No overnight street parking allowed until April
claims.supporting_quote: Collingwood's winter parking restrictions are in place

claims.claim: Blue Mountain Resort announced on November 18 an All-Inclusive Ski Week starting at $1,299 per adult, which the resort says saves more than $500 per adult versus full retail.
claims.episode_span: an All-Inclusive Ski Week starting at $1,299 per adult
claims.source_title: Blue Mountain Brings The All-Inclusive Ski Week Back To Ontario, And Every Guest Goes Home With A Season Pass
claims.supporting_quote: Blue Mountain Resort, the province’s largest mountain resort, announced on November 18 that it is bringing the format home: an All-Inclusive Ski Week that bundles three nights of accommodation, eight meals, daily lift tickets, two days of group lessons, après activities every evening and a 5×7 Pass valid for the rest of the winter, starting at $1,299 per adult.

claims.claim: Ski-week sessions run January 18 to 21 and February 15 to 18, 2027, with youth add-ons at $999 and child add-ons at $734, before HST and a 4 per cent municipal accommodation tax.
claims.episode_span: Sessions run Monday to Thursday, January 18 to 21 and February 15 to 18, 2027
claims.source_title: Blue Mountain Brings The All-Inclusive Ski Week Back To Ontario, And Every Guest Goes Home With A Season Pass
claims.supporting_quote: Two sessions run Monday to Thursday, January 18 to 21 and February 15 to 18, 2027, and the resort says the package saves guests more than $500 per adult compared with booking each piece at full retail rates.

claims.claim: Jennifer Allan-Cummings said the package takes the stress of planning off the table.
claims.episode_span: Jennifer Allan-Cummings, hospitality marketing manager, said the package takes the stress of planning off the table
claims.source_title: Blue Mountain Brings The All-Inclusive Ski Week Back To Ontario, And Every Guest Goes Home With A Season Pass
claims.supporting_quote: “The All-Inclusive Ski package takes the stress of planning off the table, making it easy to spend more time on the slopes, make new friends and experience everything that makes skiing at Blue so special.”

claims.claim: Residents named all 23 Grey County snowplows after more than 650 suggestions, with voting on Connect Grey until November 6.
claims.episode_span: Residents have named all 23 Grey County snowplows for the 2026/2027 winter after more than 650 suggestions
claims.source_title: Grey County Snowplows Hit The Road With Names Chosen By Residents
claims.supporting_quote: After more than 650 suggestions and two weeks of voting on Connect Grey, residents selected their top names for all 23 County plows.

claims.claim: Last winter Grey County operators cleared an average of 460 centimetres of snow and applied 36,000 tonnes of pre-treated salt and winter sand on 835 kilometres of highway.
claims.episode_span: cleared an average of 460 centimetres of snow last winter and applied 36,000 tonnes
claims.source_title: Grey County Snowplows Hit The Road With Names Chosen By Residents
claims.supporting_quote: Last winter, Grey County operators cleared an average of 460 cm of snow accumulation and applied a combined 36,000 tonnes of pre-treated salt and winter sand.

claims.claim: On March 8, ice broke away in Georgian Bay carrying 23 ice fishers about 2 kilometres offshore, and all 23 were brought to shore.
claims.episode_span: carried 23 ice fishers approximately 2 kilometres, in two different directions, out into the bay
claims.source_title: Ice Rescue Recognition For Grey County EMS
claims.supporting_quote: On March 8th, a rapidly evolving and life-threatening emergency unfolded in Georgian Bay when two large sections of ice broke away from shore carrying 23 ice fishers approximately 2 km in two different directions out into our bay.

claims.claim: Grey Bruce OPP Staff Sergeant Henry Thalen presented letters of commendation to Grey County paramedic responders.
claims.episode_span: each Grey County paramedic who responded received a letter of commendation
claims.source_title: Ice Rescue Recognition For Grey County EMS
claims.supporting_quote: At last week’s council meeting, Grey Bruce OPP Staff Sergeant Henry Thalen praised all who were involved. On behalf of the OPP, each Grey County paramedic responder received letters of commendation, recognizing their efforts.

claims.claim: CTV News described the Georgian Bay operation as Canada's largest ice rescue.
claims.episode_span: CTV News described the same operation as Canada's largest ice rescue.
claims.source_title: Georgian Bay, Ont., rescue crews recognized for role in ‘Canada’s largest ice rescue’
claims.supporting_quote: Georgian Bay, Ont., rescue crews recognized for role in ‘Canada’s largest ice rescue’
